subject: Meteorology
title: Lewis Fry Richardson
description: A 60-second lesson on Lewis Fry Richardson.

hook.text: In 1922, Lewis Fry Richardson published the first attempt at numerical weather prediction—computed entirely by hand.

buildup.text: He divided Europe into grid cells and tried to calculate the next 6 hours of weather using physics equations.

discovery.text: The forecast failed badly—it predicted a huge pressure change that never happened, due to a mathematical error.

twist.text: His forecast took six weeks of hand calculation—he dreamed of a 'forecast factory' with 64,000 human computers.

climax.text: His method was right, just ahead of its time—electronic computers made his vision reality just 30 years later.

punchline.text: His forecast failed—but his idea changed the world.

quiz.question: Why did Richardson's first numerical forecast fail?
options: A mathematical imbalance in the initial conditions
